answer: The cheapest real defence: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because saffron only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, quartz is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any wharf approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
